threads_text: Bloomberg reports that Anthropic is the mystery Customer B that brought in 34.5% of SpaceX's third quarter revenue, more than the US government. Claude now runs partly on Elon Musk's computers in Memphis. Is it risky for Anthropic to depend this much on Musk?

site_article.headline: Anthropic is SpaceX's largest customer, Bloomberg reports
site_article.dek: A SpaceX filing shows one unnamed client brought in 34.5% of third quarter revenue, and Bloomberg says that client is the maker of Claude.
site_article.summary: Bloomberg reported on October 29, 2026 that Anthropic is the unnamed Customer B that accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX's third quarter revenue. Anthropic rents computing power at SpaceX data centers in Memphis under contracts worth up to $120.5 billion through 2029.
site_article.seo_title: Anthropic is SpaceX's largest customer, Bloomberg reports
site_article.seo_description: Bloomberg says Anthropic is Customer B, the client behind 34.5% of SpaceX's Q3 revenue, through compute contracts worth up to $120.5 billion.
site_article.answer_summary: According to Bloomberg, Anthropic is the client SpaceX called Customer B in a regulatory filing, which accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX's third quarter revenue. Neither company has confirmed it.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic is SpaceX's largest single customer and accounted for more than a third of the company's third quarter revenue, Bloomberg reported on October 29, 2026, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report was summarized by The Next Web and Seeking Alpha.

In a regulatory filing the previous week, SpaceX disclosed that a client it identified only as Customer B produced about 34.5% of its quarterly revenue. Bloomberg identified that client as Anthropic, which would make the AI company a bigger source of income for SpaceX than the US government, long its main customer.
Anthropic declined to comment and SpaceX did not respond to Bloomberg, according to The Next Web. ShiftDelete.Net noted that neither company has publicly confirmed that Anthropic is Customer B.

Anthropic rents computing power at SpaceX data centers in Memphis, Tennessee. The capacity comes from SpaceX's AI unit, now called Super Intelligence, which sells computing power to outside customers after SpaceX took over Elon Musk's xAI business, Seeking Alpha reported.

Anthropic's own IPO filing describes computing agreements with SpaceX worth up to $120.5 billion through 2029. Payments could reach about $3.1 billion a month starting in December, according to The Next Web and Seeking Alpha. ShiftDelete.Net reported that the initial contract periods end in January and March 2027, after which Anthropic can cancel with 90 days' notice.

SpaceX's quarterly filing, submitted October 22, reported third quarter revenue of $14.575 billion, up from $5.576 billion a year earlier, and net income of $4.404 billion, ShiftDelete.Net reported. All of Customer B's revenue falls in the AI segment, which brought in $7.56 billion. A second client, Customer A, accounted for 16.6% of revenue.

The AI unit was profitable for the first time in the third quarter, according to The Next Web and Seeking Alpha. SpaceX also rents computing power to Google, which pays about $920 million a month, The Next Web reported. Seeking Alpha said Musk expects NASA, historically a major customer, to contribute less than 5% of revenue this year.

Musk has argued that SpaceX's Starlink and launch businesses make it safer than neoclouds, the companies that rent out AI computing, as lenders become more cautious about the sector. Seeking Alpha noted that the concentration of revenue in one client raises risk for investors.

The report shows how closely two companies that compete in AI models are now tied together through infrastructure. For SpaceX, a single AI lab supplying about a third of revenue is a strong growth driver and a concentration risk at the same time, since the contracts can be canceled with notice in 2027. For Anthropic, the arrangement secures large amounts of computing power from a company run by Elon Musk, whose former xAI business is now part of SpaceX.
Watch whether Anthropic or SpaceX confirms the relationship in updated IPO filings, and whether Anthropic keeps the Memphis contracts after the first cancellation dates in early 2027.
